rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one dominant stepped mass, so it passes basic morphological legibility and repair integrity. However, for neighborhood living the program contract asks for an active and legible street threshold plus a usable public void or terrace. Here the mass mostly behaves like a compact stair-stepped block with a split-wing gesture, but the open-space figure is weak and the access edge does not become a strongly public ground condition. The top view especially suggests two separated slabs with limited connective public void, while the section/silhouette remains more generic setback massing than a clearly inhabited, program-bearing terrace/court system. So it is plausible as a massing study, but not yet program-fit enough to hard pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More civic/campus-like and less street-active than a compact neighborhood living edge; do not copy the broad spread directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced low-rise massing can read as a coherent neighborhood-scale composition with connected wings and a clear shared open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too small and singular to resolve the candidate’s larger stepped mass; useful only for ground-threshold logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low pavilion can support neighborhood-commercial uses when it makes a clear entry seam and sheltered edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual in scale and waterfront condition; the candidate lacks the same depth of public void and long section sequence.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Sectional stepping can create a strong communal figure with terrace/court logic when the void is programmatically active.

The access response appears semantically weak; a stronger court/notch/ground seam would better address the verified frontage.
The stepped profile reads more like an abstract setback stack than an inhabited sectional neighborhood figure.
